limits: All benchmark records use 10,000 rows and 100 features; no multi-size dataset matrix is included.
Performance uses five repetitions, one dataset, two iterations and twelve methods; results are a same-host snapshot, not a universal leadership claim.
The controlled LightGBM gain pair uses BorutaPy and Boruta-Shap with the same LightGBM 4.7.0 configuration, importance type, data, seed and iteration/tree budgets; selector controllers differ.
Boruta-Shap with LightGBM SHAP keeps the same estimator configuration but changes attribution; comparison against gain methods is not attribution-equivalent.

Quality cross-check uses three seeds and two iterations. All methods leave signals unselected at this budget, so these records validate execution only and do not assess selection quality or convergence.
Boruta-Shap/RandomForest/SHAP remains a contextual ecosystem baseline; LightGBM SHAP quality cases are substantially faster on this host.
